subject: VPC entitlement smoothing & conversion guardrails — proposal and next steps
messages:
From: Sara Jones <sara.jones@medivex.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Medivex Procurement <procurement@medivex.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T21:05:00Z
Subject: VPC entitlement smoothing & conversion guardrails — clarification

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for walking us through Redwood Private in yesterday's demo. Two commercial questions came up in our procurement sync that I want to capture so we can evaluate packaging without losing momentum:

1) Entitlement smoothing across sites: We plan to onboard three sites over Q4–Q1 (US East, US West, EU). We need a proposal that avoids lumpy invoicing while preserving capacity guarantees — is there a way to bucket entitlements and then reallocate during the conversion window?

2) Conversion guardrails & assurance: If we convert from hosted to VPC and hit unexpected performance/regression issues, we'd like a clear remediation/resolution path (service credits / transition engineering hours). Can you outline typical assurance structures and any limits to refunds/credits?

Could you share a short commercial sketch and an example invoice cadence? Procurement would prefer something we can run past legal quickly.

Sincerely,
Sara Jones
VP, Cloud Infrastructure
Medivex Health

--
Attachment: none (we'll accept a follow-up PDF)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Jones <sara.jones@medivex.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-24T01:30:00Z
Subject: Re: VPC entitlement smoothing & conversion guardrails — clarification

Sara — really appreciate the clear ask. Quick sketch below; I attached a simple entitlement model (entitlement_smoothing_v1.xlsx) and a short Confluence note link. If this looks directionally right we can convert to a concise PDF for procurement/legal.

High-level proposal (short):
- Entitlement buckets: We propose site-level buckets (Site A/B/C) mapped to a pooled account. During the conversion window (recommended 180 days) entitlements can be reallocated across sites with a single quarterly true-up.
- Conversion window & guardrails: 180-day window with two checkpoints (30d, 90d). If performance degradations attributable to Redwood occur, Medivex receives a capped Transition Assurance Credit equal to up to 5% of the first-year Platform Fee (applies once per major release).
- Transition engineering hours: We include a 40-hour onboarding allowance for the pilot site (additional hours at standard SOW rates).
- Support tiers / SRE response: Bronze (8h), Silver (4h), Gold (2h) initial response SLA; enterprise SRE on-call options can be added for a fixed retainer.
- Invoice cadence: Monthly consumption + quarterly entitlement true-up. We can amortize a portion of the Platform Fee across the first 6 invoices if you prefer smoother OPEX.

Ask: can you confirm the three-site cadence and whether amortization across 6 months is acceptable? Happy to set a 30-min call this week.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-24T05:45:00Z
Subject: Internal: Medivex proposal — pricing levers and risk controls

Team — quick internal note before we send the formal PDF to Medivex. I reviewed Aditya's sketch and ran some sensitivity runs on the attached model. Key asks / suggested edits from pricing/legal perspective:

- Entitlement buckets: Keep three buckets but add a 10% buffer rule per-site during pilot (prevents immediate exhaustion). Allow one reallocation free during the 180-day window; subsequent reallocations trigger a $X rebalancing fee.
- Transition Assurance Credit: 5% cap is OK but add SLA trigger thresholds (p99 latency and error-rate deterioration) and a per-incident cap of 1% up to the 5% aggregate. Legal (Laura) — flag any audit/tracing requirements for attribution.
- Amortization & invoicing: Offer amortization of up to 50% of the Platform Fee across the first 6 months as an optional clause; rest billed monthly. This keeps our cash position while offering smoother OPEX for the customer.
- Support tiers: Recommend Gold include 24/7 paging for p0s and 2-weekly operational reviews for the first 90 days.

Numbers for a starter proposal (placeholder — adjust per AE):
- Annual platform fee (starter): $450,000
- Transition Assurance Credit cap: up to $22,500 (5%)
- Onboarding allowance: 40 hours included (~$12,000 value)
- Reallocation fee: $1,500 per extra bucket move after first free move

Action: Aditya — please send the customer-facing PDF with these clarifications and the example invoice cadence. Laura — can you pre-clear the SLA attribution language (audit logs, incident taxonomy)?

Thanks,
Soojin
Head of Deals, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

Subject: Medivex VPC packaging — proposal (RDW-2026-4321)

Sara — attaching a concise commercial proposal that reflects our internal conversation and options to smooth invoices. Highlights below and the PDF is attached: medivex_vpc_proposal_20260823.pdf

Summary highlights:
- Pilot & rollout: Pilot Site (US East) in Q4, then US West and EU site rollout across Q1. Pooled entitlements with quarterly true-up during a 180-day conversion window.
- Financials: Starter Platform Fee: $450k/year. Option A (amortize 50% over first 6 invoices), Option B (no amortization).
- Transition Assurance: Up to 5% of first-year platform fee (capped), with per-incident triggers tied to agreed SLA deltas.
- Onboarding: 40 hours included; additional hours billed per SOW.
- Reallocations: One complimentary reallocation during conversion window; $1,500 for additional moves.

Next steps:
1) Confirm whether you want amortization Option A or B.
2) Procurement/legal to review the attached PDF and return any redlines.
3) Proposed 30-min call Thursday 10:00am PT to align on SLA triggers.

If this directionally meets your needs we can convert into an MSA exhibit and pricing schedule.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Aditya — thank you. Procurement and Sara reviewed the PDF and it's acceptable in principle. A couple of redlines:

- Ramp window: We want a 90-day ramp where entitlements are reserved but not charged at full rate for the pilot site (50% charge), then full rate thereafter.
- SRE response: Request Gold tier initial response time be tightened from 2h to 90 minutes for P0 during the first 90 days.

We've attached our redline doc (Medivex_redline_v1.docx). If you can accept those two edits in principle we'll route to legal for a final pass.

Regards,
Medivex Procurement
procurement@medivex.com

Subject: Fwd: Medivex VPC packaging — redlines received

Forwarding Medivex redlines. Key asks from procurement: 90-day ramp (50% pilot charge) and tighten Gold P0 initial response to 90 mins for first 90 days. Medivex is otherwise OK in principle and will send to legal if we accept in principle.

My read: both asks are commercial-friendly. The ramp reduces short-term revenue but increases probability of conversion — recommend we: 
- accept the 90-day 50% pilot ramp, with a one-time onboarding engineering hour cap unchanged, and
- accept 90-minute Gold initial response for first 90 days but keep the 24/7 paging retainer optional (we should price it).

Laura — please prepare a clean exhibit that captures the amortization option and the SLA trigger language (audit log / incident taxonomies) so we can turn this to signature.

Thanks,
Aditya
